Pazapa English for Adults

Week 1 · Lesson 3 · Day 3 — Registration Forms and Asking for Help · Step 3: Pronunciation Clinic

Pronunciation Clinic

Listen, notice and try.

Écoutez, observez et essayez.

Today you practise saying your name, your telephone number and your email address clearly. You also practise polite questions when you need help.

Your privacy: You can use fictional information. Do not enter your real personal details.

Vous pouvez utiliser des informations fictives. N'entrez pas vos vraies coordonnées.

There is no score here, and no test of your accent. Take your time.

First name and last name

At a reception desk, say your first name and your last name clearly. Make the words first and last a little stronger.

Insistez un peu sur « first » et « last ».

My FIRST name is Nadia.

Mon prénom est Nadia.

My LAST name is Hassan.

Mon nom de famille est Hassan.

My first name is Nadia. My last name is Hassan.

Les deux phrases ensemble.

Now say both sentences aloud. Say your first name, then a small pause, then your last name.

Spell a name

People often ask you to spell your name. Say one letter at a time, with a small pause between the letters.

Épelez lettre par lettre, avec une petite pause.

How do you spell that? ↗

Comment cela s'écrit-il ?

N-A-D-I-A

  • N
  • A
  • D
  • I
  • A

N — A — D — I — A.

Say each letter clearly. Do not join them together.

Some letters sound similar: E and I, and M and N. Say them slowly and clearly.

Now spell a name aloud, one letter at a time.

Say a telephone number

Say a telephone number in small groups. Make a small pause after each group.

Dites le numéro par petits groupes, avec une pause.

What is your telephone number?

Quel est votre numéro de téléphone ?

  • 020group 1
  • 7946group 2
  • 0182group 3

My telephone number is 020 7946 0182.

Say: oh-two-oh — seven-nine-four-six — oh-one-eight-two.

In British English, 0 is usually said as oh in a telephone number. Two of the same number together can be said as double, for example double four.

This number is fictional. Do not give your real number here.

Say an email address

Say at for @ and dot for a full stop. Slow down at the end of the address.

Dites « at » pour @ et « dot » pour le point.

What is your email address?

Quelle est votre adresse e-mail ?

nadia dot hassan at example dot com

It is nadia.hassan@example.com.

Say: nadia dot hassan at example dot com.

If the other person does not understand, spell the difficult part: H-A-S-S-A-N.

This address is fictional. Do not give your real address here.

Polite question voice

When you ask for help, let your voice go up a little at the end. This sounds polite and friendly.

Laissez la voix monter un peu à la fin.

How do you spell that? ↗

Comment cela s'écrit-il ?

Could you repeat that, please? ↗

Pouvez-vous répéter, s'il vous plaît ?

Please speak slowly.

Parlez lentement, s'il vous plaît.

The word please is important, but the friendly sound of your voice matters just as much.

Private rehearsal

Practise the whole set. Say each line aloud. Recording is optional.

Dites chaque phrase à voix haute. L'enregistrement est facultatif.

  • My first name is Nadia.

    Mon prénom est Nadia.

  • My last name is Hassan. H-A-S-S-A-N.

    Spell the last name slowly.

  • My telephone number is 020 7946 0182.

    Three groups, with a small pause.

  • It is nadia.hassan@example.com.

    Dot, at, dot.

  • Could you repeat that, please? ↗

    Pouvez-vous répéter, s'il vous plaît ?

Clear English helps people understand you.

There is no score here, and no judgement of your accent. You practised your name, your spelling, your telephone number, your email address and two polite questions.

Un anglais clair aide les autres à vous comprendre.

Take one line with you today: Could you repeat that, please? It works at a reception desk, on the telephone and in a classroom.
